title: Sagittarius A*
subtitle: The black hole at the heart of the Milky Way
yt_title: The Monster at the Center of Our Galaxy 🌀 | Ep. 17 #shorts
description:
Episode 17 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌀
We reach the center of the Milky Way: Sagittarius A*, a black hole of 4 million suns, stars racing around it, its first image from 2022, and our 230-million-year lap around it.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 18: Next stop, the Milky Way. Our whole galaxy.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #sagittariusastar #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Episode seventeen. Next stop... the center of our galaxy.
At the center of the Milky Way hides a supermassive black hole, about twenty-six thousand light-years from us.
segments.headline: 26,000 light-years away

segments.text: It weighs about four million times as much as our Sun.
We know it's there because stars race around it. One star, S2, reaches almost three percent of the speed of light.
segments.headline: Stars racing around it

segments.text: In twenty twenty-two, astronomers released the first image of it. From here, it looks as small as a donut on the Moon.
segments.headline: First image: 2022

segments.text: Our whole solar system takes about two hundred thirty million years to go around it once.

visual.label: years for one lap around it

segments.text: Tomorrow, we zoom out and see our whole galaxy. Next stop: the Milky Way. Follow, so you don't miss episode eighteen.
